issues.failure_explanation: The event that must be lower-bounded is $\{\|z\|^2\le\rho_\delta^2/h_\delta\}$; bounding its probability from below by the chi-square concentration event $\{\|z\|^2\le d+2\sqrt{d\zeta\log(1/h_\delta)}+2\zeta\log(1/h_\delta)\}$ requires $\rho_\delta^2/h_\delta\ge d+\cdots$, but the proof asserts the opposite inequality ($\le$), which yields the wrong set inclusion. In fact, for tube radii consistent with the paper's reach framework ($\rho_t<r_t$, and Stage 2 forces $\rho_t\lesssim\beta_t h_t^3/R^3=O(h_t^2)$), one has $\rho_\delta^2/h_\delta=O(h_\delta^3)\to0$, so $\mb P(\|z\|^2\le\rho_\delta^2/h_\delta)\to0$: the noise $\sqrt{h_\delta}z$ has an $O(\sqrt{h_\delta})$ component normal to the ridge, so the end-time marginal $X_\delta=a_\delta X_0+\sqrt{h_\delta}z$ is not in such tubes and the claimed $1-e_\delta$ lower bound cannot hold at framework scales. Salvaging the argument requires $\rho_\delta\gtrsim\sqrt{d h_\delta}$, which exceeds every reach lower bound the paper establishes (it is admissible only under the false inflated reach of ISSUE-001).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reverse the inclusion (require $\rho_\delta^2/h_\delta\ge d+2\sqrt{d\zeta\log(1/h_\delta)}+2\zeta\log(1/h_\delta)$) and run the same computation with $\rho_t=\Theta(\sqrt{d h_t}\,\mathrm{polylog})$, which proves whp entry into $\sqrt{dh}$-tubes; to reconnect this entry event to Stages 2-3 one must additionally establish reach $\gtrsim\sqrt{d h_t}$ (not available from the paper's estimates) or prove early-time entry into fat tubes via an analysis of $\mc R_t$ at $O(1)$ noise levels, which the paper does not contain.
issues.overall_effect: The 'reach' stage of the reach-align-slide picture is unproven at the tube scales used by Stages 2-3; the high-probability entry guarantees of thm:informal stage 1 and thm:formal stage 1 are unsupported as written, and the entry event cannot be realized at the scales the projection machinery admits.
issues.title: Stage-1 tube-entry proof: reversed concentration inclusion; entry guarantee unavailable at framework tube scales
issues.why_classification: The broken step is local and a corrected, recognizably comparable entry theorem (at radius $\sim\sqrt{dh}$) follows from the same computation, but the corrected scale decouples Stage 1 from the tube radii the rest of the framework can handle, and an in-framework repair needs a contained but nontrivial early-time ridge analysis.

issues.failure_explanation: The Ito computation of $D_{T-t}(\Tilde Y_t)$ over $[\tilde t_{\mathrm{in}},t]$ requires $\Tilde Y_s$ to remain in the tube $\mc T_{T-s}(\rho_{T-s})$ (so that $\Pi$, $D$ are well-defined and $\|n\|\le\rho$); no confinement, stopping, or invariance argument is given, and confinement is impossible at the proof's own scale. The third-order Taylor-remainder step pins $\rho_t\le\beta_t h_t^3/(160R^3)=O(h_t^2)$, but the noise term $8d$ in the same differential inequality implies a quasi-stationary normal squared-distance of order $d/\beta_t\approx d\,h_t$, exceeding the tube capacity $\rho_t^2=O(h_t^4)$ by a factor $h_t^{-3}$: the process exits the tube in time $O(\rho_t^2)$, after which $D_{T-t}(\Tilde Y_t)$ is undefined (the nearest-point projection exists only within the reach, which the same estimates bound by $O(h_t^2)$). Moreover, at the actual fluctuation scale $\sqrt{d h_t}$ the key curvature-contraction estimate $\langle n,\nabla^2\log p_{T-t}n\rangle\le-(3/4)\beta\|n\|^2$ is unproven, since the global bound $\|\nabla^3\log p\|\approx R^3/h^3$ makes the Taylor remainder dominate the drift for $\|n\|\gtrsim h_t^2$. The theorem is thus established only under an unstated tube-confinement hypothesis that the process's own noise contradicts; it is valid as proved only for special data with globally linear ridges (e.g. two points, where the projection is global and the normal dynamics is exactly OU).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must either (i) establish direction-resolved curvature bounds for $\nabla^3\log p_t$ along the normal direction at scale $\sqrt{d h_t}$ (so that the Taylor-based contraction survives at the true fluctuation scale), together with a globally well-defined distance functional and an entry/stopping analysis, or (ii) restrict the theorem to data whose ridge geometry is globally linear/factorized (e.g. two-point data), abandoning the general-data scope.
issues.overall_effect: The normal-alignment stage of the reach-align-slide theory is not established for general data: the bound of them:normal contraciton is neither well-posed (D undefined beyond the reach) nor proven at the process's actual fluctuation scale, and the normal-error floors feeding the training-to-inference interface (thm:informal inference to training, thm:inference to training) and the RF+GD guarantees (thm:directional decomposition) inherit this.
issues.title: Stage-2 normal contraction: no tube-confinement argument, and the process provably leaves the tube where D and the curvature estimates are valid
issues.why_classification: The proof's central mechanism (curvature-based normal contraction via Taylor expansion of the score) is valid only within $O(h_t^2)$ of the ridge, a scale the diffusion noise provably exceeds by $h_t^{-3/2}$; every supported resolution requires essentially new analysis architecture or a major restriction of the advertised scope, and no comparable general-version proof is supplied by the source.

issues.failure_explanation: (i) The bound $\|r_t^{(i)}\|^2=\|\Tilde Y_t-m_{T-t}^{(i)}\|^2=O(R^2)$ is attributed to Assumption \ref{assump:data}, but that assumption bounds only the training points; membership in the center-dominant region $\mc B^{(i)}(\theta)$ is a Voronoi-type condition that does not bound the distance to the center, so the cross-term estimate $\le 8R^2a^2h^{-1}\theta$ (which needs $\|\Tilde Y_t-m^{(i)}\|\le O(R)$ pathwise) is unjustified; a moment bound on $\|\Tilde Y_t\|$ is never supplied. (ii) The claim that the frame-rotation term $2h\|P\partial_tP(I-P)\|^2\|r\|^2$ is $O(1)$ rests on $\|P\partial_tP(I-P)\|=O(\theta_t\mathrm{poly}(R,h_t^{-1}))$, justified by citing Lemma \ref{lem:important estimate} -- but that lemma controls spatial derivatives of the score on center-dominant regions, not the time derivative of the eigenframe at the moving center; the needed fact (that the frame rotation is proportional to the exponentially small minor posterior weights) is plausible but nowhere established. Without these, the stated $\Tilde\epsilon_{T-t}^{(i)}=O(d)$, and hence the theorem's final $O(d\sqrt\delta)$ bound, is unsupported. (iii) The two displays of the drift-error term also disagree in scaling ($h^{-1}\theta$ versus $h^2\eta$).

diagnostic_evidence.quote: we consider $T\in \mb{R}^{d\times d^*}$ and $N\in \mb{R}^{d\times (d-d^*)}$ to be the orthonormal basis spanning the spaces $T_z(\mc{R}_t)$ and $N_z(\mc{R}_t)$

Therefore, apply the implicit function theorem and we get: there exists a neighborhood $0\in U\subset \mb{R}^{d^*}$ and a $C^2$ map $\phi: U\to \mb{R}^{d-d^*}$ with $\phi(0)=0$ such that the local solution set to $F(u,v)=0$ is the set $\{(u,v)\mid v=\phi(u)\}$.
Therefore, a local parametrization of the manifold is $\gamma(u) = z + Tu + N\phi(u)$.

issues.failure_explanation:
The proof (i) presupposes that $\mc R_t$ is a manifold with tangent/normal spaces $T_z(\mc R_t)$, $N_z(\mc R_t)$ -- the very structure that prop:constant estimation / prop:projection-regularity claim to verify from Assumption ef{assump:data} -- and identifies $N_z(\mc R_t)$ with $\mathrm{span}(E(z))$; and (ii) applies the implicit function theorem to the frozen-basis equation $N^	op
abla\log p_t=0$ and declares the resulting local graph a parametrization of $\mc R_t$. But $\mc R_t$ is the zero set of $E(x)^	op
abla\log p_t(x)$ with $x$-dependent eigenvectors $E(x)$; the frozen-basis zero set is a different set in general (their tangents at $z$ differ by terms involving $DE\cdot
abla\log p$, which are non-negligible at ridge points where the score is nonzero, e.g. asymmetric transition-zone points). Hence the second-fundamental-form bound is established for the wrong set, and the verification that $\mc R_t$ is a piecewise $C^2$ submanifold with positive reach under Assumption ef{assump:data} is not validly established.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redo the local analysis with the varying eigenfield: at each $z\in\mc R_t$ with a spectral gap, show that the full derivative of $x\mapsto E(x)^\top\nabla\log p_t(x)$ is surjective (bounding the $DE\cdot\nabla\log p$ term, e.g. near critical points of $\log p_t$ where it vanishes, or under an explicit gap-and-score smallness condition), conclude that $\mc R_t$ is locally a $C^2$ graph, and derive the second-fundamental-form bound for the true tangent spaces.
issues.overall_effect: The foundational geometric inputs of the tube/projection framework (validity of Assumption \ref{assump:ridge set} for empirical data, the reach lower bound, the $\|\nabla\Pi_t\|$ and $\|\partial_t\Pi_t\|$ bounds) lack a valid proof; the stage theorems, stated only under Assumption \ref{assump:data}, implicitly rely on this unestablished verification whenever they use $\Pi_t$, $D_t$, or the tube machinery.
issues.title: Ridge manifold / second-fundamental-form verification freezes the eigenbasis and derives the bound for the wrong local set
issues.why_classification: The manifold property and a curvature bound of the same order are plausibly true and repairable by a contained but genuinely new local analysis handling the varying eigenvectors; no global restructuring is needed, but the current proof establishes the bound for a different set and cannot be fixed by a constant or notation change.
